hints.concept: Think about what the last valid index of an array should be.
hints.guidance: An array with length n usually has valid indexes from 0 up to n - 1.
hints.targeted: Check whether this loop condition should stop before the array length instead of including the length value.

hints.concept: A condition should normally check a value rather than change it.
hints.guidance: Look at the operator inside this condition and decide whether it is comparing two values.
hints.targeted: Check whether the condition uses assignment where a comparison was intended.

hints.concept: Array length tells you how many items exist, not the last valid position.
hints.guidance: Compare the number of elements with the final usable index.
hints.targeted: Check whether the array length is being used directly as an index.

hints.concept: Strings are objects, so == asks whether two variables point to the same object, not whether the text matches.
hints.guidance: Think about the difference between comparing object references and comparing the characters inside two strings.
hints.targeted: Check whether this comparison should use the .equals() method instead of == or !=.

hints.concept: A loop only finishes when its counter eventually makes the condition false.
hints.guidance: Follow the counter value for a few iterations and see whether it moves toward or away from the loop bound.
hints.targeted: Check whether the update step moves the counter in the direction the condition expects.

hints.concept: A return statement immediately ends the method; nothing after it in the same block can run.
hints.guidance: Trace the method line by line and note the exact point where execution leaves the method.
hints.targeted: Check whether the statements after this return were meant to run before it.

hints.concept: In a switch, execution continues into the next case unless something like break stops it.
hints.guidance: Walk through what happens after this case's statements finish and which case runs next.
hints.targeted: Check whether this case should end with a break before the next case begins.

hints.concept: A semicolon on its own is a complete, empty statement.
hints.guidance: Look closely at what the condition actually controls when a semicolon comes right after the closing parenthesis.
hints.targeted: Check whether the semicolon right after the condition should be removed so the block below belongs to it.

hints.concept: An assignment stores the value on the right into the variable on the left.
hints.guidance: Compare both sides of this assignment and think about what actually changes after it runs.
hints.targeted: Check whether one side of this assignment should be a different variable or expression.

hints.concept: An OR condition is true when at least one side is true.
hints.guidance: Pick a few sample values for the variable and evaluate each side of the OR to see if the whole condition can ever be false.
hints.targeted: Check whether this condition should combine the two checks with && instead of ||.

hints.concept: Strings in Java never change; their methods build and return a brand-new string.
hints.guidance: Think about where the new string produced by this method call actually goes.
hints.targeted: Check whether the result of this call should be assigned back to a variable.

hints.concept: Dividing an integer by zero is not a number Java can produce; it stops the program instead.
hints.guidance: Look at the value on the right side of this division or modulo operation.
hints.targeted: Check whether the divisor here should be something other than 0.

hints.concept: A loop's condition is checked before the first iteration; if it is false, the body never runs.
hints.guidance: Plug the starting value of the counter into the condition and evaluate it by hand.
hints.targeted: Check whether the starting value and the loop bound are the wrong way around.

hints.concept: In an if / else-if chain, only the first branch whose condition is true will run.
hints.guidance: Compare each condition in this chain and think about which branch handles which situation.
hints.targeted: Check whether this repeated condition should test a different value or range.

hints.concept: A while loop only stops when something inside the loop makes its condition false.
hints.guidance: List the variables used in the condition and find the line inside the loop that changes any of them.
hints.targeted: Check whether the loop body should update the variable used in the while condition.
